title: Director Service Accounts (m/f/d)
description:
Director Service Accounts @ Sereact 🦾

Director Service Accounts (m/f/d) · Stuttgart, with frequent travel to customer sites across Europe · Reports to the VP Operations · Full-time

Who we are

Sereact builds the robot brain for physical work. Cortex, our vision-language-action foundation model, is hardware-agnostic: the same model runs single-arm and dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators that pick, sort and handle returns in live production across Europe and the US. Customers include Zalando, IKEA, BMW, Rohlik and DHL.

Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles.

Why this role, why now

The Site Acceptance Test is where a deployment ends and a customer’s operation begins. From that day our robots pick in someone else’s building, every shift, against targets the customer measures. Many of our customers buy Sereact as a service: they pay for robots that work, not for robots that were delivered.

Our deployments are growing from single robots to fleets, and the site that performs is the site that grows. We now want one leader who owns every live site from SAT on: keeps it at target, brings it everything we ship in software and hardware, speaks for the customer inside Sereact, and turns a working site into a growing one.

The Real-World Learning Loop runs through your sites

Cortex learns from live deployments. Every station at a customer is part of that loop, so a station that is down is more than a service problem: a cell sitting dark is a stopped sensor.

  • In-Situ Policy Execution. Every live station runs the current policy in a real operation. Your surface on it: each site at target, every shift.

  • Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own work while they run. Your surface on it: stations that run and stay connected, so the data keeps coming.

  • Data Curation and Learning. Failures and edge cases decide what Cortex learns next. Your surface on it: what your sites tell us reaches engineering and research with the context they need.

  • Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies pass validation gates before they return to the fleet. Your surface on it: they land in your customers’ operations on a schedule the customer can plan around, with a way back if something is off.

A site that runs well teaches Cortex more, and it grows.

Responsibilities

  • Take over every site at SAT. Set the standard for what a site needs before your team takes it on: documentation, open points, spare parts, contacts and targets. If a site is not ready, it stays with deployment until it is.

  • Keep every site at target. Own each site’s performance against its contract: availability, throughput and pick success. See a problem coming before the customer does, and run the recovery plan when a site falls behind.

  • Run planned change. Software releases and model updates reach customer operations in a rhythm customers can plan around: release notes, change windows, blackout periods, validation on site and a rollback path.

  • Run hardware updates and retrofits across the installed base, from new gripper generations to station upgrades and fixes, with Hardware Engineering and the field teams, without stopping the customer’s operation.

  • Get every site ready for peak: hypercare and coverage plans for the weeks that matter most to our customers, from Black Friday to the January returns wave.

  • Be the customer’s advocate inside Sereact. Bring their priorities into product, R&D, hardware and operations, make sure what we promised at SAT holds, and own the customer communication when something goes wrong.

  • Take each site from SAT to expansion with Strategic Accounts: the performance evidence, the site capacity and the technical plan for the next stations. Strategic Accounts own the contract; you make the expansion ready to happen.

  • Report site health customers trust: one view of every site, monthly performance reports and the operational part of every business review.

  • Build and lead the Service Accounts team: Service Account Managers who each own a portfolio of live sites, and a playbook that still works when the installed base is ten times larger.

  • Work hand in hand with Deployment, Technical Support & Field Service, Hardware Engineering, R&D and Strategic Accounts, so a live site gets one coordinated answer, not five.

Not in scope, by design

  • Deployment up to SAT stays with our deployment teams. You set the bar for what you take over.

  • Incidents, the support desk, field technicians and spare parts logistics stay with Technical Support & Field Service. You own the site; they own the ticket.

  • Contracts, pricing and the expansion deal itself stay with Strategic Accounts. You make the case; they sign it.

  • Product and hardware design stay with engineering. You bring them what the field needs.

What makes this role hard

  • Every change to a live operation is a risk, and not changing is a risk too: the fleet only gets better if updates reach it. You make both safe.

  • Our robots work in other people’s buildings: their WMS, their conveyors, their shift patterns, their peak. Much of what decides a site’s performance is not ours, and it is still your problem.

  • You sit between the customer and our teams. Sometimes the customer’s priority is not ours. You argue for it, or you explain honestly why not.

  • The installed base grows faster than any team. What works by heroics today breaks at ten times the size.

Your first 12 months

  • First 90 days: know every live site and its people; one named owner, one health view and a clear status against target for each; a handover standard at SAT agreed with deployment.

  • By month 6: releases and retrofits in a rhythm customers can plan around; peak season run on hypercare plans; account plans with Strategic Accounts for the largest customers; the first Service Account Managers hired.

  • By month 12: every site at target or on a dated recovery plan; expansions coming out of the installed base; a playbook ready to take to the US.

What you bring

  • 8+ years owning live installations of complex automation after go-live (warehouse automation, intralogistics, robotics or comparable 24/7 systems), as service account manager, technical account manager, customer success or service delivery lead, including at least three years leading a team.

  • You did it while the installed base grew from tens to hundreds of sites, and you built the processes rather than inheriting them.

  • Technical enough to read a log, follow a root cause and hold your own with engineers. Commercial enough to sit with a customer’s operations director and talk performance, cost and growth.

  • You have run releases, upgrades and retrofit programs in live operations without stopping them.

  • Customers trust you because you tell them early and you tell them straight.

  • Fluent English and German; another European language is a plus.

  • You are happy to spend a large part of your week at customer sites.

Nice to have: subscription or Robotics-as-a-Service models · goods-to-person and AS/RS integrations · e-commerce, returns or grocery fulfilment · experience in both a scale-up and an established automation vendor.

Not the right fit: account management without technical depth, or running a ticket queue without ever owning a customer.

Three questions we will ask you

  1. Tell us about a live site that fell behind its targets. What did you change in the first two weeks, and how did it end?

  2. A customer’s peak starts in four weeks. Engineering wants to ship a model update and a gripper retrofit before then. What do you do?

  3. How do you know a site is about to grow, or about to leave, before the customer tells you?

What we offer

  • A fleet in live production that grows every month, and the mandate to build the team that keeps it at target.

  • A key role in the operations leadership of a company scaling from Europe into the US, with equity.

  • Travel, accommodation and meals covered when you are on site.

  • Our HQ in Stuttgart, with teams in Zurich and Boston.

How we hire

Conversations with our VP Operations and the founders, a working session on a real case from one of our live sites, and time with the team in Stuttgart. We move fast.

title: Director Solutions (m/f/d)
description:
Director Solutions (m/f/d) · Stuttgart, with frequent travel to customer sites in Europe and the US · Reports to the CEO · Full-time

Who we are

Sereact builds the robot brain for physical work. Cortex, our vision-language-action foundation model, is hardware-agnostic: the same model runs single-arm and dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators that pick, sort and handle returns in live production across Europe and the US. Customers include Zalando, IKEA, BMW, Rohlik and DHL.

Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles.

Why this role, why now

A robot deal is won twice: once when the contract is signed, and once when the cell runs the customer’s orders at the throughput we promised. The distance between the two is decided before anyone unpacks a crate: by the site survey, the item spectrum, the cell concept, the integration with the customer’s warehouse systems, and by the number we write into the contract.

We are moving from single stations to fleets, with customers who order dozens of systems at once. The deals are getting larger, the sites more varied, and a concept that does not fit the site is paid for in months of commissioning. We are looking for the technical counterpart to our sales team: a leader who sits next to every account executive from the first conversation and makes deals technically feasible. Someone who has deployed robots personally, knows what a real site does to a design, finds the solution that makes the customer’s use case work, and makes sure what we promise is what we can build.

The Real-World Learning Loop starts with your design

Cortex learns from live deployments. The cell you design is the body the model works in, and a concept that goes live in weeks instead of months is weeks of real-world data no one else has.

  • In-Situ Policy Execution. Every station runs the current policy on the customer’s items. Your surface on it: reach, camera placement and item presentation that let the policy do its job on day one.

  • Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own work while they run. Your surface on it: standard cells with a known stack wherever possible, so every pick teaches the same model.

  • Data Curation and Learning. Edge cases decide what Cortex learns next. Your surface on it: the item spectrum and the sample tests you run before signature, so curation starts before go-live.

  • Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies return to the fleet after validation. Your surface on it: concepts that transfer, so a policy proven on one cell works on the next.

A site designed right goes live faster, teaches Cortex more, and grows.

Responsibilities

  • Be Sales’ technical counterpart on every deal. One solutions lead next to every account executive, from the first customer conversation to signature. Your job is to make the deal technically feasible: understand the customer’s process, find the solution that works for their site and items, and give Sales a technical story the customer’s engineers believe.

  • Own the technical solution for every deal, from the first site visit to the signed scope: site survey, process and material-flow analysis, item spectrum, cell concept and layout, reach and camera study, integration concept for WMS, WCS and conveyors, safety concept. One package per deal, and you are accountable for it.

  • Set the number. Throughput, pick success and intervention rates we commit to per site, derived from the item spectrum and the site and checked against what comparable live sites actually do. No KPI goes into a contract without your sign-off.

  • Standard first. Configure our standard single-arm, dual-arm and mobile products to the site. Every deviation is a documented decision taken with Engineering, not a discovery during installation.

  • Run the gate. No contract is signed without your solution design sign-off and a delivery slot agreed with Operations. You hold the pen on the technical statement of work, the acceptance criteria and the site-readiness list the customer has to meet.

  • Make it feasible, fast. Sample tests, pick studies and scanning or dimensioning checks with our applied AI team, within days, not months. When a requirement does not fit, find the version that does: a different cell or item presentation, a phased scope, a pilot that proves the hard part first. A no is the last answer, not the first.

  • Hand over to Deployment a package that builds: layout, configuration, integration spec, acceptance criteria, risks and dates, so commissioning executes without reopening the concept. You stay accountable until the first live orders prove the design.

  • Own the interfaces to integrators and WMS vendors at the solution level, from AutoStore and goods-to-person systems to conveyor and WMS partners: interface specs, a clear split of responsibilities and readiness tests before we ship.

  • Build the solution library: reference designs per use case (goods-to-person ports, put walls, returns, decanting, store replenishment), throughput models, layout templates and integration patterns, so the tenth deal of a kind takes a day, not a month.

  • Close the loop from the field. What commissioning and live sites learn about a design flows back into the reference concepts and into requirements for Product and Engineering.

  • Lead the big pursuits in person: the technical counterpart to the customer’s engineering and operations teams in fleet deals, tenders and RFPs; demos and reference visits with the customer’s real items.

  • Build and lead the Solutions team in Europe and the US: solutions engineers who have stood at a cell, with the playbooks and tools (CAD, simulation, throughput models) to do this at ten times today’s deal flow.

  • Partner with Sales, Operations and Deployment, Service Accounts, Systems Engineering, Applied AI and Supply Chain. Report to the CEO and be part of the leadership team.

Not in scope, by design

  • Pricing, contract terms and closing stay with Sales. You are their technical counterpart: you own what we promise technically, how we make it work and when it can be delivered.

  • Build, installation and commissioning up to the Site Acceptance Test stay with Operations. You hand over a package that builds, and you stay accountable for the concept.

  • Live sites after acceptance stay with Service Accounts. You design for the site they will have to run.

  • Product and system design stay with Engineering and New Product Introduction. You configure the standard; what the standard lacks, you bring them as requirements.

What makes this role hard

  • Your job is to find the yes we can deliver. Most of the time that means a smarter solution, sometimes a different scope or a later date, and occasionally a no to a deal the company wants. When it is a no, you have to be right about it, with numbers.

  • The product moves fast: what the model could not do in spring it may do in autumn. You commit to today’s capability and plan for tomorrow’s, and you do not confuse the two.

  • The site is never finished. WMS, conveyors, bins and item master data belong to the customer or an integrator, and your design has to survive their reality.

  • Every shortcut in the concept comes back as months of commissioning. You carry both sides of that trade, in front of Sales and in front of Deployment.

Your first 12 months

  • First 90 days: every open deal has a solution package and a realistic commitment; the gate is in place (checklist, sign-off, delivery slot); every live site’s concept reviewed for what we would design differently today.

  • By month 6: reference designs for our three main use cases; a throughput model validated against live sites; interface specifications agreed with our three most important integration partners; the first solutions engineer in the US onboarded.

  • By month 12: deals signed in 2027 go live at the throughput in the concept, without redesign; a Solutions team in Europe and the US; a library that makes the standard deal routine.

What you bring

  • 8+ years in warehouse or factory automation, several of them in solutions, application engineering or deployment of robotic systems. You have personally deployed robots in live operations, from site survey to commissioning: piece-picking arms, dual-arm cells, mobile manipulators or AMR fleets. You know what a go-live night feels like.

  • You did it while your company grew from its first sites to dozens or hundreds, and you built the solution process rather than inheriting it.

  • You can do the work yourself: a site survey, a layout in CAD, a material-flow and throughput model, an interface specification for a WMS or WCS (APIs, PLC handshakes), a risk assessment for a cell. And you can explain it to a customer’s operations director and to our machine learning engineers in the same afternoon.

  • You have worked side by side with sales teams as their technical counterpart and helped win deals by finding a solution that works. You have led solutions or application engineers, and when a sales team pushed for a bigger number, you held the line with evidence.

  • You know the intralogistics ecosystem: AutoStore and goods-to-person systems, conveyors, the integrators; ideally e-commerce, returns or grocery fulfilment.

  • Fluent English; German is a strong plus, since many of our customers are in the DACH region. You are happy to spend a large part of your time at customer sites in Europe and the US.

Nice to have: piece-picking or dual-arm robotics · systems whose capability is driven by machine learning and moves every quarter · robotics-as-a-service models · deployments in the US.

Not the right fit: pre-sales architects who have never commissioned a system, solutions as slide-making, or anyone who needs a finished product specification before they can start.

Three questions we will ask you

  1. Walk us through a site you designed that went live at the throughput you promised, and one that did not. What was the difference?

  2. Sales wants to sign a deal this quarter with a KPI 50% above what your model says the site can do. What do you do in the next 48 hours to still make the deal work?

  3. A customer’s goods-to-person ports are fixed, and the layout leaves 30 cm less reach than our standard cell needs. What are the options, and which one do you choose?

What we offer

  • A product in live production with some of Europe’s largest operators, and the mandate to decide what we promise and what we build.

  • A seat in the leadership team of a company scaling from Europe into the US, with equity.

  • Travel, accommodation and meals covered when you are on site.

  • Our HQ in Stuttgart, with teams in Zurich and Boston.

How we hire

Conversations with the founders and our VP Operations, a working session on a real site (we give you a layout, an item spectrum and a target; you tell us what to build and what to promise), and time with the team in Stuttgart. We move fast.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer
description:
YOUR MISSION

 

A software engineer today uses Claude Code or Cursor. A mechanical engineer designing the next jet engine still searches Excel sheets and asks whoever has been around longest.

 

We are building the AI co-engineer for physical products: one that works natively in 3D and learns from real engineering decisions. We are in production with major European manufacturers, with real revenue and customers who tell us when we are slow.

 

The problems are open ones. Getting an agent to reason usefully about geometry, making 3D search work on real customer part libraries, and figuring out what the interface even looks like when an engineer asks why a bracket failed. There is research to borrow from and very little product to copy.

 

Senior or staff level depending on experience.

 

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 

You will own large problems end to end, across the stack. We cannot say exactly what that looks like in month three, but here is what the last two years have actually involved.

 

  • A multi-agent orchestration SDK, built from scratch. Nothing off the shelf handled what we needed: long-horizon execution that runs for hours and survives restarts.

  • CAD conversion as a real pipeline. It used to be manual and brittle. Turning it into production infrastructure meant writing a Python wrapper around a C++ SDK and making it reliable enough to sit under everything else.

  • Migrating the application off Electron and Webpack onto SSR React with Vite. That architecture is what the whole product now sits on.

 

What is coming:

 

  • 3D-to-3D search across real customer part libraries, not benchmark datasets

  • Constraint solvers and optimization, and getting an agent to use one sensibly

  • Agents that hold a useful model of a physical object, which is still an open problem

  • Hybrid cloud deployments for manufacturers who cannot send their data anywhere

 

We work in Python and TypeScript, with multi-agent orchestration and AI integrations across several providers.

 

WHAT WE CARE ABOUT

 

  • You have shipped production systems across frontend and backend, and can point at them

  • Your CV reads as a set of problems, not a stack

  • You use AI heavily to go faster, but you built things the hard way first

  • You are fine when the problem is not yet defined

  • You deliver end to end, and you are still there when it needs maintaining

 

Bonus: CAD, computational geometry, constraint solving or optimization, 3D, LLM agents, industrial software. None required.

title: Head of Product | Intch
description:
About Intch

Intch is a professional social network with a marketplace for part-time work. You can think of it as a professional network built for senior specialists who take on meaningful contracts alongside their main work. A typical contract lasts from three to six months. The product is used in 140 countries and is available in up to 20 languages. Intch has fewer than 40 people and four product areas, with three already live and one preparing to launch. Intch is rethinking how people and companies find each other and build trust online.

What you’ll do

  • Own the B2C product end to end, including its P&L.

  • Set the product direction and own the 3–6 month roadmap across strategy, experimentation, and delivery.

  • Drive growth through hypothesis-driven experiments and measurable improvements in acquisition, activation, and retention.

  • Own the product metrics and use data to guide decisions and prioritisation.

  • Conduct CustDev interviews and build a deep understanding of user behaviour across a global, multilingual audience.

  • Partner with the B2B product teams to make the B2C product the connective layer across Intch’s product ecosystem.

  • Report directly to the founder and CEO and take over the product vertical they currently lead. There is no CPO at Intch: all product owners report to the CEO, so this is the most senior product position in the company.

What you need to succeed

  • 5+ years of experience in product management.

  • A strong B2C growth track record, including experiments, acquisition, and measurable results.

  • Proven experience scaling a product that already has strong product–market fit.

  • A strong record of improving key metrics such as growth, activation, and retention.

  • Strong product sense and a hypothesis-driven approach to problem-solving.

  • Comfort working with data and translating insights into action.

  • Experience working in a startup or another fast-moving, high-ownership environment.

  • High autonomy, accountability, and comfort working without micromanagement.

  • Fluent Russian.

What you get

  • Full ownership of a profitable, fast-growing product and its P&L, reporting directly to the founder.

  • A deliberately compact team (under 40 people) where everyone has a large area of ownership and streamlined collaboration.

  • Metrics-driven culture: every function, including support and payments, owns numbers. Your P&L is your scoreboard.

  • Flat, cross-pollinating structure: anyone in the company can bring a validated idea to your product. You can do the same across other verticals.

  • Paid vacation and sick leave.

title: Privacy & Product Counsel
description:
This role can be office-based in Freiburg, Germany/ San Francisco, USA or remote-first, with a requirement to be in the office one full week per month.

About Black Forest Labs

We’re the team building the foundational layer for visual intelligence: multimodal models trained jointly on images, video, audio, and action to see, generate, and understand the world.

Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, the breakthroughs that made generative AI accessible to millions. With FLUX, we're pushing into generative media at scale, machines that act in the physical world, and emerging applications in computer use.

Our FLUX models top public benchmarks and run in production in some of the world's biggest platforms. We're a small, fast growing research lab competing with the largest companies in the world. From our labs in Freiburg to San Francisco, we're building what comes next.


Why This Role

Every FLUX release, API feature and enterprise offering requires legal oversight. Black Forest Labs’ (BFL) frontier technologies raise questions where there is no established precedent – especially as we push further into video, perception and physical AI.

We’re hiring a Privacy & Product Counsel to find solutions and help drive our product teams forward. You’ll sit in our Legal, Policy & Assurance (LPA) team and be embedded with research, product and engineering, shaping how BFL builds and ships.

This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to build a privacy function at the frontier of AI and robotics.

What You’ll Work On

  • Product counselling. Be the go-to lawyer for product teams on new models, API features and innovative products, from first spec to launch, giving clear, risk-calibrated advice that keeps us shipping.

  • Marketing. Partner with our Growth, Marketing and DevRel teams to review launch announcements, model cards and campaign copy so that our claims about FLUX are accurate. Advise on privacy matters relating to product marketing, analytics, commercial and creator partnerships, and advertising claims.

  • Privacy by design. Own BFL’s GDPR programme across the model lifecycle: training data, fine-tuning, inference, logging and retention. Run point on DPIAs and privacy documentation as required.

  • Customer commitments. Partner with GTM on DPAs, zero-data-retention and no-training terms, security questionnaires and enterprise negotiations – and work with the team to ensure that what we promise matches what we do.

  • International transfers and vendors. Manage EU–US transfer mechanisms (SCCs, the EU–US Data Privacy Framework and TIAs), and run privacy diligence on sub-processors and AI tooling.

  • US privacy. Track and implement obligations under US state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA and peers) and emerging AI-specific state legislation.

  • Regulatory interface. Prepare BFL for engagement with data protection authorities, and handle data subject requests, complaints and incidents, including breach assessment and notification.

  • Policy and documentation. Draft and maintain privacy notices, internal policies, records of processing and the privacy elements of compliance documentation.

  • Scale the function. Build playbooks, templates and training so the rest of BFL can handle routine privacy questions without you.

What We’re Looking For

  • 5–8 years’ PQE as a qualified lawyer in an EU/EEA jurisdiction or the UK, with a substantial focus on data protection and product counselling

  • Experience at a technology company, in a top-tier law firm’s privacy or tech practice, or both – ideally including time in-house advising product teams directly

  • Deep, practical command of the GDPR (and the German BDSG), the ePrivacy framework and international transfer rules, plus a working knowledge of how other relevant EU regulations, such as the EU AI Act, interact with them

  • Familiarity with US privacy and AI law (CCPA/CPRA, BIPA, and state AI and deepfake statutes)

  • A track record of advising on AI, ML or data-intensive products: you understand training pipelines, inference and feature releases well enough to ask engineers the right questions

  • Comfort giving direct, pragmatic advice under uncertainty – you can turn a novel legal question into a clear recommendation and workable product guidance

  • Strong drafting skills across DPAs, privacy notices, DPIAs and commercial privacy terms

  • Excellent written and spoken English; you can explain complex issues to researchers, executives and regulators alike

  • An ownership mindset and low ego: you’re comfortable in a fast-moving, high-growth environment where you build processes, not just follow them

While not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

  • Experience with generative AI, computer vision or media products – particularly involving biometric data, likeness rights or synthetic media

  • Direct experience engaging with data protection authorities or the EU AI Office

  • CIPP/E, CIPT or equivalent certification

  • German language skills

  • An interest in adjacent areas such as security and trust & safety


How We Work Together

We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. You’ll be based in Europe or the US and work from your home location, with one week each month spent with us in Freiburg / San Francisco to stay connected with the team.

Everything we do is grounded in four values:

  • Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.

  • Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.

  • Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

  • Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.

Closing

If this sounds like work you’d enjoy, we’d love to hear from you.


Compensation

EU: €150,000 - €200,000 + equity
US $200,000 - $250,000 USD

Note: We may use AI-assisted tools to help organize applications. All hiring decisions are always made by our team.

title: Paid Search Consultant
description:
About Making Science

Making Science is an international digital acceleration company with over 1,200 experts across 15 markets, including Spain, Portugal, Mexico, Colombia, France, Italy, the UK, Ireland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Germany, Georgia, and the USA. As a proud consulting partner of Local Planet — the world’s premier network of independent media agencies — we deliver a suite of digital, technology, and performance marketing services to a global clientele. Our expertise spans digital marketing and MarTech, software and cloud solutions, artificial intelligence, and SaaS, all underscored by a relentless pursuit of innovation.

Making Science was ranked 15th in the FT1000: Europe's Fastest-Growing Companies 2023. Committed to making a positive impact, Making Science actively engages in various ESG initiatives. We’ve joined forces with the Climate Pledge, the United Nations Global Compact, and Pledge1%, dedicating resources and efforts to support non-profit organizations. Through these endeavors, we are committed to driving meaningful change for a brighter, more sustainable future.

As part of its commitment to innovation, Making Science offers its clients end-to-end capabilities required for consulting, development, integration, and maintenance of advanced IT solutions. Our global network of delivery hubs not only fosters job growth but also serves as an incubator for cultivating top-tier tech talent, fueling projects that accelerate transformation and modernisation.

Our team is composed of experienced digital professionals, who have a wide knowledge in the different stages and disciplines of the digital transformation: Digital Strategy, Infrastructures, Software Development, Creativity and UX/UI Design, Digital Marketing, and Big Data.

Making Science is People Centric, and we actively bet on our employees! We believe that they are the key to any successful business, and therefore, our greatest asset. We strive to provide daily learning opportunities for those who work with us and their colleagues. It is also really important that they enjoy what they do, and have positive experiences. We want our employees to feel proud of their accomplishments, and that they belong to a company that is in constant growth, because each person’s contribution is essential to achieve our success.

We believe in the power of diversity and the value of inclusion. At Making Science, our unique experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives are what drive our innovation and success. We are dedicated to providing an equitable hiring process and an inclusive work environment where all individuals are respected and feel they belong. Join us and bring your whole self to work!

Some details about your department

The Advertising Department guarantees an increase in the volume of our clients' businesses through advertisements on different platforms: search engines, social media, affiliation, media, programmatic, among others (Google Ads, Facebook Ads, Instagram Ads, Twitter, LinkedIn, Amazon, Microsoft Advertising, Programmatic, Affiliation, Media). We always work in the different phases of our clients' Customer Journeys. Our DNA is to rely on innovation and technology to be efficient with our clients' investments, and to know how to direct messages to potential users at the right place and at the right time. Measurement is key, because it allows us to reach our clients' business data.

In Advertising, we are not about words, we are about results. Since we are a large team, we always work to promote teamwork and learning from each other. We welcome challenges with a smile on our faces, and we believe that our positive energy promotes good results for our clients.We are a winning team, and we have a great time working as a team. We always challenge ourselves, to foster professional and personal growth.

What we’d like you to do

  • Act as a strategic consultant to different national and international large accounts for all their SEM Strategies.

  • Create strategies on the main searchers. Create, manage and track search Ads campaigns on Google Ads, Search Ads 360 and Bing Ads.

  • Design AI testing roadmaps and implement custom automation scripts.

  • Manage Business Manager and other platforms in depth.

  • Work closely with the clients to define objectives and follow-up on agreed roadmaps.

  • Maintain daily communication with the clients to review campaigns, results, and propose innovative strategies. Participate actively in meeting with clients.

  • Responsible for seeking efficiency and resolving it through process improvement and implementation of new technologies or improvement in their use

What we’d like you to bring

  • We are looking for someone who is proactive and eager to learn, with the ability to adapt to new challenges with a positive attitude.

  • At least 4 years of experience performing similar tasks in other marketing agencies or clients, focused on the execution and management of Paid Search campaigns, leveraging Generative AI (Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude) to optimize ad copy and strategy.

  • Strong proficiency in visual Generative AI tools (Midjourney, Nano Banana) to conceptualize and create high-quality creative assets for campaigns.

  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize tasks and manage multiple simultaneous requests across projects, using automation workflows (Zapier, Make, N8N) to reduce manual workload.

  • Technical familiarity with AI development environments (Google AI Studio) and RAG tools (NotebookLM) to build custom solutions and manage knowledge bases efficiently.

  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with a strategic mindset and a hands-on approach to tackling challenges utilizing Agent Space and LLMs.

  • Strong analytical skills, with a knack for working with data and generating insights supported by AI models.

  • Excellent communication and client management skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with both internal teams and clients.

  • Experience in project coordination and management, with a keen eye for detail.

  • You have a C1 level of English, both spoken and written.

  • Fluent in German both spoken and written.

Nice to have / Plus:

  • Strong proficiency in visual Generative AI tools (Midjourney, Nano Banana) to conceptualize and create high-quality creative assets for campaigns.

  • GA4: Basic and Advanced Concepts for Cross-Channel and Business-Level Analysis.

Perks of joining us

  • Modern central office

  • Creative outreach

  • Team spirit and community atmosphere

  • Training and coaching

  • Talent training and onboarding from our employees

  • Transparent culture

  • Transportation ticket subsidy

  • Gym membership subsidy

  • International exchange (LocalPlanet)

  • Gifts for anniversaries and at the end of probationary period.

  • Parties and team events

  • Social engagement

title: Projektleiter MSR / Gebäudeautomation (m/w/d)
description:
Sie suchen anspruchsvolle Projekte in der Gebäudeautomation, wollen aber abends trotzdem zu Hause sein? Hier übernehmen Sie TGA-Großprojekte ab 1 Mio. € und profitieren von hervorragenden Arbeitsbedingungen und einem familiären Umfeld.

Sie wünschen sich kurze Entscheidungswege, wollen aber auf die Stabilität und das Netzwerk eines Großkonzerns nicht verzichten? Eine geregelte Arbeitswoche ohne ständige Überstunden und bis zu 35 freie Tage klingen nach dem perfekten Ausgleich für Sie? Dann erwartet Sie hier ein attraktives Jahresgehalt von 75.000 bis 85.000 € je nach Erfahrung sowie ein Firmenwagen auch zur privaten Nutzung.

Ihr neuer Arbeitgeber ist ein etablierter, eigenständiger TGA-Vollausrüster mit rund 160 Mitarbeitenden und einem starken Mutterkonzern im Rücken. Das Leistungsspektrum deckt alle Gewerke von der Konstruktion bis zur Ausführung ab. Der Fokus liegt auf anspruchsvollen Großprojekten im Industrie-, Gewerbe- und Sonderanlagenbau. Sie erwartet ein wertschätzendes Umfeld, in dem Handschlagqualität zählt und man sich über alle Standorte hinweg persönlich kennt.

Bewerben Sie sich jetzt auf diese unbefristete Stelle als

Projektleiter MSR / Gebäudeautomation (m/w/d) | bis 85.000 € brutto/Jahr + Firmenwagen | Halle (Saale)

Ihre Perspektive

  • Karriere & Entwicklung: Ein strukturierter Karrierepfad steht für Sie bereit. Perspektivisch können Sie die Leitung des Subteams für Gebäudeautomation am Standort übernehmen.

  • Work-Life-Balance & Freizeit: Flexible Arbeitszeiten auf Vertrauensbasis und der Abbau von Mehrstunden über zwei bis drei Brückentage im Jahr sorgen für Ausgleich. Zusammen mit 30 Urlaubstagen und bezahlten Freistellungen an Heiligabend sowie Silvester kommen Sie auf theoretisch 35 freie Tage.

  • Mobilität & Ausstattung: Sie erhalten einen Firmenwagen, bei dem auch eine Umstellung auf ein E-Fahrzeug möglich ist. Diesen können Sie uneingeschränkt privat nutzen. Ein Smartphone und ein Laptop gehören zur Standardausrüstung.

  • Echte Teamkultur: Flache Hierarchien und Kollegialität auf Augenhöhe prägen den Arbeitsalltag. Gemeinsame Sommerfeste, Weihnachtsfeiern und regelmäßige Standort-Events stärken den Zusammenhalt.

  • Finanzielle Extras: Neben Ihrem Festgehalt profitieren Sie von einer jährlichen Leistungsprämie sowie tariflichem Weihnachts- und Urlaubsgeld. Eine arbeitgeberfinanzierte betriebliche Altersvorsorge sichert Sie zusätzlich ab.

Ihre Aufgaben

  • Sie leiten und steuern eigenverantwortlich anspruchsvolle Projekte in der MSR-Technik und Gebäudeautomation.

  • Sie planen, koordinieren und überwachen alle Projektphasen von der Vergabe bis zur erfolgreichen Inbetriebnahme.

  • Sie führen Ihre internen Projekt- und Montageteams und steuern externe Nachunternehmer zuverlässig.

  • Sie behalten die Kosten-, Termin- und Qualitätsziele fest im Blick und erstatten regelmäßig Bericht an die Bereichsleitung.

  • Sie erstellen und prüfen souverän Leistungsverzeichnisse, Angebote sowie Nachträge.

  • Sie stimmen sich eng mit Bauherren und Fachplanern ab und koordinieren die Schnittstellen zu Elektro- und IT-Gewerken.

Ihr Profil

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium der Elektrotechnik, Automatisierungstechnik, Versorgungstechnik oder Gebäudeautomation

  • Oder alternativ ein erfolgreicher Abschluss als Techniker oder Meister in einem einschlägigen Bereich

  • Mehrjährige fundierte Erfahrung in der Abwicklung von Projekten in der Gebäudeautomation, Gebäudeleittechnik oder MSR-Technik. Engagierte Bauleiter aus diesem Umfeld, die den nächsten Schritt in die Projektleitung gehen möchten, sind ausdrücklich willkommen.

  • Gutes technisch-kaufmännisches Verständnis, insbesondere im Nachtragsmanagement und bei Kostengruppen

  • Sicheres Basiswissen bezüglich relevanter Normen und Richtlinien wie VOB und HOAI

  • Kenntnisse in gängigen Planungstools und GA-Systemen (wie z. B. iTWO, DEOS, Beckhoff oder Siemens) sind ein Plus

  • Deutsch: C1

  • Bundesweite Reisebereitschaft für ein bis zwei Baustellentage pro Woche bei maximal einer Übernachtung

  • Strukturierte, lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise gepaart mit Kommunikationsstärke und Hands-on-Mentalität

Ihre Bewerbung

Interessiert? Bewerben Sie sich jetzt unkompliziert bei Ihrem Ansprechpartner Christopher Zinow. Ihre Beratung durch Riverstate ist für Sie selbstverständlich kostenlos. Der Bewerbungsprozess ist schlank gehalten: In der Regel findet nur ein einziges Gespräch direkt mit der Fachabteilung und der Geschäftsführung statt.

title: SAP S/4HANA Sales & Distribution Consultant Inhouse (m/w/d)
description:
Raum München, Vollzeit · unbefristet

Für unseren Mandanten, eine international tätige, börsennotierte Industriegruppe, suchen wir einen SAP S/4HANA Sales & Distribution Consultant (m/w/d), der die Vertriebsprozesse in der laufenden S/4HANA-Transformation fachlich verantwortet und den Implementierungspartner steuert.

Die Gruppe führt ihre Gesellschaften in mehreren Ländern schrittweise auf ein gemeinsames SAP-Template. Das Template steht, der erste Rollout wird vorbereitet. • Sie verantworten die Vertriebs- und Auftragsprozesse im Template, vom Angebot über Preisfindung und Lieferung bis zur Faktura.

• Sie übersetzen Anforderungen der Vertriebsbereiche in Lösungen nah am SAP-Standard.

• Sie bereiten Pilot und Rollouts aus Vertriebssicht vor und sind bei wichtigen Meilensteinen vor Ort.

• Sie bringen Entscheidungen und Risiken klar auf den Punkt, auch gegenüber Programm- und IT-Leitung.

• Sie machen die Anwenderinnen und Anwender im Vertrieb fit für die neuen Abläufe.

• Im bestehenden System sind Sie Ansprechpartner für knifflige Fälle und für angebundene Systeme, etwa für Zoll und Versand.

Das bringen Sie mit

• Mehrjährige Erfahrung mit SAP Sales & Distribution, inhouse oder in der Beratung

• Mehrere S/4HANA-Projekte, die Sie in Ihrem Modul von der Konzeption bis zum Go-live getragen haben, idealerweise mit Rollouts in mehrere Länder

• Tiefes Verständnis der Vertriebsprozesse inklusive Preisfindung und der Verbindungen zu Materialwirtschaft und Finanzen

• Erfahrung mit Implementierungspartnern und die Sicherheit, deren Vorschläge fachlich zu bewerten

• Klare Kommunikation auf Leitungsebene, Selbststeuerung und einen kühlen Kopf in Phasen mit hohem Takt

• Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch und fließendes Englisch

• Von Vorteil: Erfahrung mit SAP ECC, Projektleitungserfahrung, Kenntnisse in Außenhandelssoftware mit SAP-Anbindung

Das erwartet Sie

• Arbeitsplatz im Raum Augsburg, München, Münster oder Essen: drei Tage pro Woche am Standort, zwei Tage mobil, dazu projektabhängige Reisen innerhalb der Gruppe

• Eine Fachrolle mit echtem Einfluss auf ein langfristiges Programm und ein SAP-Team mit rund zehn Kolleginnen und Kollegen

• Festanstellung in einer wirtschaftlich soliden Gruppe mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen

• Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, flexible Arbeitszeiten und Weiterbildung

Interesse?

Senden Sie uns Ihren Lebenslauf mit Gehaltsvorstellung und frühestem Eintrittstermin. Stefan Schulz meldet sich bei Ihnen für ein vertrauliches Erstgespräch.

title: Client Sales Director (m/f/d)
description:
Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

GET TO KNOW US

At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we're on a mission to make every company a wellness company.

We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you'll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally. 

Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

We're hiring a Client Sales Director to lead one of our Client Enterprise Sales teams in Germany. You will manage and develop a senior team of Sales Managers, providing coaching and mentorship, shaping deal strategy, supporting high-stakes negotiations, and designing complex commercial initiatives. You'll build strategic partnerships with enterprise prospects, leading consultative sales cycles and crafting solutions tailored to their specific challenges.

Beyond team leadership, you'll act as a cross-functional connector, partnering closely with Marketing, Product, Operations, Finance, Legal, Revenue Operations, and Customer Success to ensure strategic alignment, remove roadblocks, and accelerate outcomes.

This is more than a job. It's a high-impact opportunity for professional and financial growth, with competitive, performance-based compensation. It's ideal for collaborative, entrepreneurial leaders who thrive in dynamic environments and value long-term customer relationships.

 

YOUR IMPACT

  • Enterprise Deal Execution & Commercial Acumen: Proven track record of navigating complex, multi-stakeholder SaaS sales cycles, building data-driven ROI business cases, and consistently closing six-figure enterprise contracts.
  • Pipeline Generation & Regional Territory Health: Demonstrates proactive outbound prospecting, tight collaboration with SDR partners, and rigorous pipeline inspection to maintain high forecasting accuracy and predictable revenue growth.
  • Executive Presence & Stakeholder Management: Commands high-level conversations with C-suite and senior HR/Total Rewards leaders, establishing credibility, handling objections effectively, and building lasting strategic partnerships.
  • Cross-Functional Orchestration: Effectively aligns cross-functional internal resources—including onboarding, legal, and product teams—to ensure seamless deal execution and post-sale client success.
  • Product Mastery & Solution-Selling: Articulates Wellhub's market value proposition clearly, translating product capabilities and case studies into bespoke executive solutions tailored to enterprise pain points.
  • Industry Representation & Network Expansion: Actively expands Wellhub's regional footprint and brand authority through targeted networking, industry event engagement, and relationship building within the HR community.
  • Mission Alignment & Culture Contribution: Exemplifies a commitment to workplace wellbeing, modeling sustainable high performance, collaborative empathy, and strong alignment with Wellhub's core mission.
  • Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life wellness.

 

WHO YOU ARE

  • Leadership & People Management: Proven experience leading and coaching senior sales managers and high-performing SaaS teams, cultivating a culture of accountability, operational rigor, and consistent quota achievement.
  • Enterprise Revenue Growth: Track record of driving new business acquisition and closing high-value, complex deals, ideally within SaaS, HR consulting, or corporate benefits environments.
  • Executive Presence & Stakeholder Influence: Exceptional ability to build trusted relationships with C-level buyers, navigate intricate decision-making units, and align cross-functional partners to drive strategic outcomes.
  • Data-Driven Strategy & Pipeline Execution: Highly analytical approach to sales metrics and forecasting, leveraging CRM insights to optimize team performance, identify growth levers, and maintain predictability.
  • Persuasive Communication & Fluency: Professional business and technical English fluency, with strong acumen in delivering executive-level presentations, financial business cases, and consultative narratives.
  • Sales Tech & Modern Prospecting Acumen: High technical proficiency across modern sales stacks (e.g., Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, SalesLoft) to scale pipeline generation and streamline sales workflows.
  • Growth Mindset, Agility & Client Centricity: Proactive, outcome-oriented approach with a strong commitment to continuous learning, client advocacy, and navigating change in high-growth, fast-paced environments.

We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. For this specific role, please note that prior experience leading senior sales teams, driving new business growth, and successfully securing significant contracts with complex organizations and advanced English are mandatory requirements.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life. Our benefits include:

WELLHUB:  Free Gold membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you.

FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer hybrid and remote options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role can be discussed with your recruiter and hiring manager. We offer all employees a one-time reimbursement to set up their home office equipment and a monthly work allowance to help cover the costs of working from home. Our offices are in Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Portugal, Romania, Spain, and the UK. You can work from any office or remotely based in any of these countries.

FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE:  Flexibility for us isn't just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

PAID TIME OFF: We know how important it is to take time away from work to recharge. Employees receive 30 days paid holiday per year in addition to annual holidays (including an extra holiday on your birthday!).

PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. We offer 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. Parents giving birth are eligible for an extended leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while they get settled.  

CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions,  build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success. 

CULTURE: You'll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here. 

Want to see what it's really like to work here? Follow us on Instagram @lifeatwellhub and watch our team video on YouTube!

 

Diversity, Equity, and Belonging at Wellhub

We aim to create a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive space where everyone knows they belong. At Wellhub, we welcome and celebrate your authentic self.

Wellhub is committed to creating a diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other basis covered by appropriate law.

Our commitment to inclusion also extends to how we recognize and reward our people. We're proud to be Syndio Fair Pay Certified, reflecting our ongoing dedication to equitable and fair pay practices across our global team. Read more about it here.

Questions on how we treat your personal data? See our Job Applicant Privacy Notice.

title: Teamleitung Naturnaher Wasserbau / Gewässerentwicklung (m/w/d)

Hier machst du dein Ding. Und wenn es passt, wird es auch deins.

Du planst Renaturierungen, Hochwasserschutz, Gewässerentwicklung. Fachlich macht dir so schnell keiner was vor. Was oft fehlt, ist der Raum dafür: Über dein Projekt entscheidet am Ende jemand, der nie am Gewässer stand, dein Budget verantwortest du nur auf dem Papier, und mit dem Kunden spricht jemand anderes.

Selbst wirksam werden. Bei Stowasserplan führst du dein eigenes Team, steuerst deinen Bereich wirtschaftlich und sprichst selbst mit deinen Auftraggebern. Du entscheidest, wie ihr arbeitet, und siehst direkt, was deine Entscheidungen bewirken. Nicht weil wir die besseren Ingenieure wären, sondern weil wir kurze Wege haben.

Schrittweise einsteigen. Wir suchen keine Führungskraft auf Zeit. Wer sich bei uns gut anstellt, unternehmerisch denkt und Verantwortung übernehmen will, kann sich nach einer Einarbeitungs- und Bewährungsphase am Unternehmen beteiligen und diese Beteiligung Schritt für Schritt ausbauen. So profitierst du direkt von dem Wert, den du mit deinem Team schaffst. Bei uns führt ein Weg von der Teamleitung zur Mitgesellschafterin oder zum Mitgesellschafter.

Wer wir sind

Stowasserplan plant seit 2009 naturnahen Wasserbau: Renaturierung von Fließgewässern, nachhaltiger Hochwasserschutz, Starkregen- und Erosionsvorsorge, Revitalisierung von Auen. Ingenieurbiologische Bauweisen sind unsere Kernkompetenz, nicht ein Zusatz im Leistungsverzeichnis.

Wie das aussieht, wenn es gelingt: Am renaturierten Pleißenbach spielen heute Kinder am Wasser. Am Hoyerswerdaer Schwarzwasser ist der Eisvogel zurück. Von der Machbarkeitsstudie über die Objektplanung nach HOAI bis zur Umweltbaubegleitung machen wir das komplett selbst.

Mit unserem Schwesterunternehmen Stowasserservice entwickeln wir aus unserer Praxiserfahrung Software, mit der andere Büros und Verwaltungen arbeiten: PROGEMIS für das Gewässermanagement, SOFIE für die Ingenieurbiologie. KI nutzen wir zunehmend als Werkzeug in unseren Planungsabläufen. Die fachliche Verantwortung bleibt beim Menschen.

Was du übernimmst

  • Ein Team von fünf bis acht Leuten: Projektverantwortliche, Projektmitarbeitende, Praktikanten. Du führst sie, planst Kapazitäten, führst die Mitarbeitergespräche und arbeitest neue Leute ein.
  • Die wirtschaftliche Steuerung deines Bereichs: Budgets, Termine, Qualität, Nachträge. Nach der Einarbeitung entscheidest du im vereinbarten Rahmen ohne Rücksprache.
  • Die Kundenbeziehung. Du sprichst selbst mit den Gewässerverantwortlichen in Städten und Verbänden, schreibst Angebote, verhandelst und holst Folgeaufträge.
  • Der Teil, für den uns heute die Zeit fehlt: KI-gestütztes Arbeiten in Prozesse einbauen, die halten. Projektstandards, Vorlagen, Qualitätssicherung, Wer das kann, prägt hier die nächsten Jahre.

Was du mitbringst

  • Führungserfahrung. Du hast mehrere Jahre eigenständig Projekte in Flussbau, Ingenieurbau, Wasserwirtschaft oder Regenwassermanagement geleitet und dabei Verantwortung für Menschen übernommen. Du weißt, wie man Aufgaben verteilt, Menschen entwickelt, Konflikte klärt und Entscheidungen auch dann trägt, wenn sie unbequem sind.
  • Du führst gern. Es macht dir Spaß, wenn dein Team besser wird, nicht nur, wenn dein Projekt gut läuft. Gespräche mit deinen Leuten siehst du als Teil deiner Arbeit, nicht als Unterbrechung. Begeisterte Kunden sind dein Maßstab.
  • Ein Studium im Bereich Bauingenieurwesen / Wasserbau, Landschaftsarchitektur, Umwelt- oder Landschaftsplanung oder etwas Vergleichbares.
  • HOAI sitzt, Baustelle ist dir vertraut, und im Vergaberecht (VgV, UVgO, VOB/A) kennst du dich sicher aus, als Bieter wie bei der Vorbereitung von Bauvergaben.
  • Praktische KI-Erfahrung. Du nutzt KI-Werkzeuge bereits im Arbeitsalltag, etwa für Recherche, Texte, Auswertungen oder Angebote, kennst ihre Grenzen und hast Lust, das mit deinem Team weiterzuentwickeln.

Naturnahen Wasserbau und Ingenieurbiologie musst du nicht mitbringen. Das ist unser Kernwissen, und wir bringen es dir bei. Dafür nehmen wir uns Zeit und planen es ein.

Was du bekommst

  • Entscheidungen, die du triffst, statt Entscheidungen, die du vorbereitest.
  • 60.000 bis 70.000 Euro, je nach Erfahrung.
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit, an ein bis zwei Tagen pro Woche im Homeoffice zu arbeiten.
  • Fortbildung, die wir bezahlen und für die du Arbeitszeit bekommst.
  • Ein Büro, das wächst. Wir gehen in die DACH-Region. Das schafft Aufgaben, die es heute noch nicht gibt.
  • Eine unternehmerische Perspektive: Wenn die Zusammenarbeit trägt, kannst du dich schrittweise am Unternehmen beteiligen.

Warum es diese Stelle gibt

Wir wachsen. Dafür bauen wir unseren Führungskreis aus und besetzen eine weitere Teamleitung in Vollzeit.

Du kommst nicht in ein fertiges Team, sondern in eines, das gerade neu sortiert und erweitert wird. Wer darin die Chance sieht, ist hier richtig.

title: Senior Executive Assistant (PSA-3)
description:
United Nations University (UNU)

The United Nations University (UNU) is a global think tank and postgraduate teaching organization within the United Nations System. UNU engages in policy-relevant research, capacity development, and knowledge dissemination in furtherance of the purposes and principles of the United Nations. The work of UNU contributes to solving pressing global problems that are the concern of the United Nations and its Member States. 

For the past five decades, UNU has been a source of impartial research on sustainability, human security, and economic development. With hundreds of researchers working at institutes in 12 countries, UNU's expertise spans the full breadth of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, generating policy-relevant knowledge to effect positive global change. UNU collaborates closely with other UN entities and leading research institutions across the globe. For more information, please visit http://unu.edu.

The United Nations University Vice-Rectorate in Europe (UNU-VIE), established in 2007 in Bonn, Germany, is one of two UNU Vice-Rectorates and the only one located in Europe. It supports the institutional development of UNU, facilitates collaboration across UNU and the UN, as well as fosters strategic partnerships - particularly with the Global South - and shares knowledge and expertise through the development of joint activities and projects. In addition, UNU-VIE conducts frontier research reinforcing existing UNU programming and supporting the implementation of key UN priorities. More information about UNU-VIE can be found here: https://unu.edu/vie.

.

Responsibilities

Under the authority of the Vice-Rector in Europe and Director of UNU-EHS and the direct supervision of the Head of the Executive Office & Special Assistant to the Vice-Rector and Director of UNU-EHS, the incumbent will be entrusted with the following tasks:

1.  Manage appointments and mission travel for the Vice-Rector/Director of UNU-EHS and Deputy Director, if required

  • Manage the calendar of the Vice-Rector/Director, and Deputy Director, as requested, including scheduling internal and external appointments;

  • Welcome and assist visitors to the Office of the Vice-Rector/Director, liaising with UN Security;

  • Coordinate official travel and accommodation arrangements in accordance with applicable UN and UNU rules and procedures.

 

2.  Support internal and external communications

  • Serve as a communication focal point for relevant UNU offices, UN agencies and external stakeholders in Bonn and internationally;

  • Screen telephone calls/enquiries/requests and route them as appropriate;

  • Monitor the institutional functional mailboxes, responding to enquiries and forwarding as appropriate;

  • Prepare correspondence, reports and meeting minutes in English, German and other UN languages if required;

  • Prepare presentations, handouts, and statistics as required.

3.    Support logistical arrangements for institutional meetings and events

  • Support the organization of major academic and administrative events including managing the booking of accommodation, hospitality, and travel to and from Bonn;

  • Support the identification of possible venues on and off campus for the respective events;

  • Manage the booking of UNU Bonn’s conference and meeting rooms and respond to participant requests.

4.     Provide support with general office administration

  • Maintain institutional archives and filing systems;

  • Update and maintain an overview of all institutional contacts;

  • Procure office supplies for the Office of the Vice-Rector/Director;

  • Assist in identifying and liaising with potential vendors for Executive Office events, inter alia.

 

5.     Perform other duties as assigned by supervisor

Key Performance Indicators

  • Timely and accurate coordination of calendars, appointments and official travel arrangements;

  • Timely response to internal and external enquiries, including an appropriate choice of language to the respective audience;

  • Accurate, clear and timely preparation of correspondence/written documents, such as letters, briefing notes, meeting minutes, ppt presentations and others;

  • Effective assistance with logistical arrangements for meetings and institutional events;

  • Timely updating, completeness and accuracy of institutional archives and the contact database, including records of key partners, key stakeholders and other relevant institutional contacts;

  • Timely procurement of supplies and vendors.

Competencies

Values:

  • Inclusion - Take action to create an environment of dignity and respect for all, regardless of age, culture, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, geography, grade, language, nationality, racial identity, religion, sex, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, social origin or any other aspect of identity;

  • Integrity - Act ethically, demonstrating the standards of conduct of the United Nations and taking prompt action in case of witnessing unprofessional or unethical behaviour, or any other breach of UN standards;

  • Humility - Demonstrate self-awareness and willingness to learn from others;

  • Humanity - Act according to the purposes of the United Nations: peace, dignity and equality on a healthy planet.

Behaviours:

  • Connect and Collaborate - Build positive relationships with others to advance the work of the United Nations and work coherently as One UN;

  • Analyse and Plan - Seek out and use data from a wide range of sources to understand problems, inform decision-making, propose evidence-based solutions and plan action;

  • Deliver Results with Positive Impact - Hold oneself and others accountable for delivering results and making a positive difference to the people and causes that the United Nations serves;

  • Learn and Develop - Pursue own learning and development and contribute to the learning and development of others;

  • Adapt and Innovate - Demonstrate flexibility, agility and the ability to think and act in novel ways.



1) Education and certification:

Secondary education diploma OR First degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in International Management/Business Assistant, Business Communication, International Relations, European Secretarial Studies, Office Management, or related field.

2) Required qualifications and experience:      

  • For candidates with a secondary education diploma, at least four (4) years of relevant experience in office, secretarial or administrative support is required. For candidates with a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field, at least three (3) years of relevant experience is required. Experience in an international or multi-ethnic working environment is required;

  • Experience of drafting written documents (e.g. presentations, briefings, meeting minutes) is required;

  • Proficiency in Microsoft applications including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access is required.

3) Desired qualifications and experience:

  • Experience in event management;

  • Knowledge of contact databases/knowledge management systems;

  • Strong ability to establish priorities, work within tight timelines and multi-task; excellent organizational skills; strong interpersonal skills; resilience;

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively and professionally with internal and external stakeholders.

4) Language Requirements:

  • Fluency in English and German, both oral and written, is required;

  • Knowledge of another UN official working language is an asset.

Remuneration

The successful candidate will be employed under a national PSA contract. UNU offers an attractive compensation package including an annual net salary, commensurate with the experience and qualifications of the candidate. Benefits include 30 days annual leave and a health insurance scheme.

UNU is not liable for any taxes that may be levied on the remuneration you receive under this contract. Payment of any such taxes remains the sole responsibility of PSA holders.


Duration of contract

The duration of the initial contract is 1 year. This is Personnel Service Agreement (PSA) contract with UNU, with the possibility for renewal subject to requirements and satisfactory work performance. The combined duration on a PSA contract with UNU may not exceed six (6) years. The mandatory age of retirement for PSA holders is 65 years.  This post is open to applicants from all countries and UNU will aid the
successful applicant in securing a work visa for Germany, as necessary. It is, however, a locally recruited post and no relocation allowances
apply. The duty station will be Bonn, Germany.


Starting date: As soon as possible


How to Apply

To apply to UNU, you will not need an account. Instead, we ask that you:

  • Fill out the UNU P11 Form (please avoid using similar forms provided by other United Nations organisations);

  • Provide a motivation statement (in the P11 form);

  • Provide a CV (max. 2 pages);

  • Provide a cover letter (max. 1 page) setting out how the qualifications and experience match the requirements of the position;

  • Answer a few questions that are tailored to the position; and

  • apply via the apply link;

You may wish to refer to the UN Values and Behaviours Framework for more information.


Application Deadline: 03 December 2026.

Submissions must be received by 23:59 CET on the deadline; late entries will not be accepted.


Assessment

Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by a competency-based interview, background checks, and references.


Special Notice

PSA holders are neither “staff members” under the Staff Regulations and Rules of the United Nations nor “officials” for the purpose of the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations (1946). They are subject to the Rector's authority and may be assigned to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations University. The Rector reserves the right to appoint a candidate at a level below that advertised. UNU is committed to diversity and inclusion within its workforce, and encourages all candidates, irrespective of gender, nationality, religious and ethnic backgrounds, including persons living with disabilities to apply and become part of the organisation. Applications from developing countries, and from women are strongly encouraged. Eligible internal applicants are also encouraged to apply. UNU has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNU, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination. If you have supervisory function, you need to have awareness on gender related issues.


Information about UNU rosters

UNU reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNU at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.


Scam Warning

UNU does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

Die hairfree GmbH ist Marktführer für dauerhafte Haarentfernung¹ in der DACH-Region. Mit über 70 Standorten in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz sowie mehr als 100 Mitarbeitenden gehören wir zu den führenden Anbietern im Bereich ästhetischer Dienstleistungen.

Seit über 20 Jahren verbinden wir professionelle Beratung, innovative Behandlungskonzepte und echte Leidenschaft für Beauty. Unser Ziel ist es, Menschen zu einem neuen Hautgefühl zu verhelfen, sicher, individuell und mit höchstem Qualitätsanspruch.

Bei hairfree erwarten dich klare Strukturen, moderne Prozesse, ein starkes Team und echte Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten.

Deine Rolle

Du hast Freude am Verkauf, begeisterst Menschen und möchtest Verantwortung für einen Standort übernehmen? Dann komm zu hairfree in Rosenheim.

In unserer Lounge verbindest du persönliche Kundenberatung mit aktivem Vertrieb und Teamführung. Du hörst aufmerksam zu, erkennst individuelle Wünsche und empfiehlst die passende Behandlungslösung. Dabei begleitest du Interessierte vom ersten Gespräch bis zum Vertragsabschluss.

Gleichzeitig entwickelst du deine Lounge gemeinsam mit deinem Team weiter. Du setzt Prioritäten, unterstützt deine Mitarbeitenden und behältst eure Vertriebsziele im Blick.

Das Beste: Du arbeitest mit vorqualifizierten Anfragen von Menschen, die bereits Interesse an dauerhafter Haarentfernung¹ haben. So kannst du direkt an ihren Bedürfnissen anknüpfen und dich auf persönliche Beratung und erfolgreiche Abschlüsse konzentrieren.

Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Festgehalt plus ungedeckelte Provisionen: Du erhältst ein verlässliches Grundgehalt und verdienst an deinem Verkaufserfolg mit.

  • Verantwortung und Gestaltungsspielraum: Du bringst eigene Ideen ein und gestaltest die Entwicklung deines Standorts aktiv mit.

  • Strukturierte Einarbeitung: Du lernst unsere Leistungen, Beratungsabläufe und Systeme Schritt für Schritt kennen.

  • Regelmäßige Vertriebscoachings: Unsere Academy und interne Trainings stärken dich in Beratung, Verkauf und Führung.

  • Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten: Du baust deine Fähigkeiten aus und kannst bei entsprechender Eignung weitere Verantwortung übernehmen.

  • Abgestimmte Arbeitszeiten: Wir planen deine Einsätze gemeinsam und passend zu den Kundenterminen.

  • Kurze Entscheidungswege: Du stehst im direkten Austausch mit der Vertriebsleitung und kannst Fragen schnell klären.

  • Ein kollegiales Team: Gegenseitige Unterstützung, gemeinsame Erfolge und Mitarbeiterevents gehören bei uns dazu.

  • Moderne Arbeitsumgebung und gute technische Ausstattung.

  • Mitarbeiterrabatte und Vergünstigungen.

  • Gute Erreichbarkeit und Parkmöglichkeiten.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Kunden beraten und gewinnen: Du führst persönliche Beratungsgespräche, erkennst Bedürfnisse und begeisterst Kundinnen und Kunden für die passende Behandlung.

  • Verkäufe abschließen: Du erklärst Angebote verständlich, beantwortest Fragen und führst Interessierte verbindlich bis zum Vertragsabschluss.

  • Kontakte nachfassen: Du bleibst an offenen Anfragen und Angeboten dran, klärst Rückfragen und vereinbarst konkrete nächste Schritte.

  • Deinen Standort steuern: Du behältst Umsatz, Vertriebskennzahlen und Terminauslastung im Blick und leitest passende Maßnahmen ab.

  • Dein Team weiterentwickeln: Du unterstützt deine Mitarbeitenden im Vertriebsalltag, gibst regelmäßig Feedback und arbeitest mit ihnen an gemeinsamen Zielen.

  • Verlässliche Abläufe sichern: Du sorgst dafür, dass Kundenanfragen zeitnah bearbeitet und unsere Beratungsstandards eingehalten werden.

  • Informationen dokumentieren: Du pflegst Gespräche, Termine, Angebote und Vereinbarungen sorgfältig in unserem digitalen System.

  • Verbesserungen mitgestalten: Du tauschst dich mit der Vertriebsleitung und anderen Standorten aus und bringst Ideen für bessere Abläufe und eine persönliche Kundenbetreuung ein.

Und das Beste: Mit einer persönlichen Einarbeitung, regelmäßigen Trainings und fachlichem Austausch unterstützen wir dich dabei, sicher und erfolgreich in deine Rolle hineinzuwachsen.



  • Freude am Verkauf: Du berätst mit Überzeugung, gehst auf Fragen ein und begleitest Interessierte aktiv bis zum Vertragsabschluss.

  • Gespür für Menschen: Du hörst aufmerksam zu, erkennst Bedürfnisse und baust mit deiner offenen, empathischen Art Vertrauen auf.

  • Interesse an Beauty: Haut, Ästhetik und dauerhafte Haarentfernung¹ begeistern dich. Du möchtest unsere Leistungen kennenlernen und verständlich vermitteln.

  • Klare Kommunikation: Ob persönlich, am Telefon oder im Team: Du trittst freundlich, professionell und verbindlich auf.

  • Organisationstalent: Du behältst Kontakte, Angebote und Termine im Blick und fasst offene Themen zuverlässig nach.

  • Verantwortungsbewusstsein: Du möchtest deinen Standort voranbringen, gemeinsame Ziele erreichen und dein Team im Alltag unterstützen.

  • Lernbereitschaft: Du nimmst Feedback an und hast Lust, dich in Verkauf, Beratung und Führung weiterzuentwickeln.

  • Idealerweise passende Erfahrung: Du hast bereits im Vertrieb, in der Kundenberatung, im Einzelhandel, in Beauty, Kosmetik, Fitness oder einer anderen Dienstleistungsbranche gearbeitet. Erste Führungserfahrung ist ein Plus.

Du kommst aus einer anderen Branche? Auch als Quereinsteiger (m/w/d) bist du willkommen, wenn du Verkaufstalent mitbringst und bereit bist, Verantwortung zu übernehmen. Wir unterstützen dich mit einer strukturierten Einarbeitung und regelmäßigen Trainings.
