title: Sales Manager CH, KI-Software für Psychotherapeut:innen
description:
Über VIA HealthTech

VIA macht aus einer Therapiesitzung ein fertiges Sitzungsprotokoll und aus Sitzungsprotokollen vollständige psychologische Berichte. Arbeit, die Therapeut:innen bisher mehrere Stunden pro Woche gekostet hat.

Wir sind die marktführende KI-Assistenz für Psychotherapeut:innen. Über 4.000 Psychotherapeut:innen im DACH-Raum nutzen VIA, wir verarbeiten Hunderttausende Sitzungen pro Monat. Wir sind nach ISO 27001:2022 zertifiziert und verfügen über ein BSI-C5-Testat.

Wir sind ein multidisziplinäres Team in Berlin-Mitte. Marktführer in Deutschland zu sein, ist erst der Startpunkt. Die Schweiz ist unser nächster Markt, und du baust ihn mit auf.

Die Rolle

Du bist unsere erste Person im Schweizer Markt. Du baust die Pipeline von Grund auf, entwickelst das Playbook und führst es selbst aus.

In Deutschland läuft unser Funnel vor allem über Webinare: Therapeut:innen melden sich an, testen VIA 14 Tage und buchen selbst. Du findest heraus, was davon in der Schweiz funktioniert und was anders laufen muss: Qualifizierung am Telefon, Cold-Calling, andere Outbound- und Inbound-Kanäle, Verbände, Weiterbildungsinstitute, grössere Organisationen als eigener Kanal. Du testest, misst und skalierst, wo der Hebel am grössten ist.

Du arbeitest eng mit Marketing an Zielgruppen, Kampagnen und Botschaften für den Schweizer Markt und gibst direkt zurück, was im Gespräch wirklich zieht.

Die Rolle ist senior gedacht. Wenn du mid-level, aber aussergewöhnlich schnell und hungrig bist, bewirb dich trotzdem.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Den Markt öffnen. Du identifizierst die wichtigsten Zielgruppen in der Schweiz: selbstständige psychologische Psychotherapeut:innen, Psychiater:innen, Organisationen der psychologischen Psychotherapie, Ambulatorien und Kliniken. Du priorisierst, wo wir zuerst gewinnen.
  • Leads in Kund:innen verwandeln. Qualifizierungsgespräche, Webinare, Demos, Follow-up während der Testphase, Abschluss. Du bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für Schweizer Kund:innen.
  • Neue Kanäle erschliessen. Berufsverbände wie FSP, ASP und SBAP, Weiterbildungsinstitute, Fachveranstaltungen und Kongresse. Erstansprache per Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn, wo sie sich lohnt.
  • Playbook bauen, während du verkaufst. Was konvertiert, welche Einwände in der Schweiz wirklich kommen (etwa zu Datenschutz und Datenhaltung), welche Sequenz funktioniert.
  • Zahlen verantworten. Deine KPIs entlang des Funnels, gemeinsam mit unserem Commercial Engine Lead, der Tracking und Infrastruktur baut.
  • Sales-Enablement-Material. Du passt an, was zum Verkaufen und Vermarkten in der Schweiz am besten wirkt, von Sprache bis Preisdarstellung in CHF.
  • Feedback ins Produkt bringen. Was Schweizer Kund:innen brauchen und woran Deals scheitern, besprichst du direkt mit dem Produktteam.

Dein Profil

Must-have

  • Nachgewiesene Abschlüsse im B2B-Vertrieb in der Schweiz, idealerweise SaaS oder Digital Health, belegbar in Zahlen
  • Echte Hunter-Mentalität. Du hast bereits aktiv Erstkontakte am Telefon gemacht und hast damit kein Problem. Wenn dich 40 Gespräche am Tag abschrecken, ist das die falsche Rolle
  • Kenntnis des Schweizer Gesundheitswesens oder die Fähigkeit, dich sehr schnell einzuarbeiten: Grundversicherung, Anordnungsmodell, Rolle von Kantonen und Verbänden

  • Systemdenken. Du baust reproduzierbare Prozesse statt Einzelfälle, mit dem Ziel, dass dein Ansatz auch ohne dich funktioniert

Von Vorteil

title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer (Remote)
description:
This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations.

If you've built something before, start here

The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day.

What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day.

What you'll do

You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with.

  • Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket.

  • Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved.

  • Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on.

  • Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate.

  • Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix.

  • Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people.

What success looks like after 3 months

  • There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version

  • You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations

  • At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need

  • You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users

  • You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both

  • You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data

  • You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is

  • You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title

  • Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going

  • You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls

  • You make things simpler over time, not more clever

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement

You probably won't enjoy it if

  • You just want to code and go home

  • You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit

  • Ambiguity and chaos bother you

  • You want a well-defined backlog handed to you

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount

Our stack

Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

  1. Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

  2. Technical deep-dive call: walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong.

  3. Meet Scalera Day: join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team.

  4. Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

Working at Scalera

  • Remote within the EU or EEA

  • Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success

  • Competitive compensation

Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.

title: Senior AI/ML Engineer
description:
This role is also open to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations.

If you've built something before, start here

Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on.

We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them.

What you'll own

You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means:

  • Training and fine-tuning: embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data.

  • Document understanding: models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs.

  • Product matching: retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products.

  • Evaluation: offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse.

  • Training and serving infrastructure: automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production.

  • Customer problems: when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it.

What success looks like after 3 months

  • There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next.

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version.

  • A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results.

  • Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed.

  • You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own.

  • You've decided at least one thing we should stop building.

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users.

  • You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data.

  • You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail.

  • You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure.

  • You measure before you believe, and a single aggregate score doesn't convince you.

  • You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is.

  • You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title.

  • Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going.

  • You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls.

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement.

You probably won't enjoy it if

  • You just want to code and go home.

  • You don't like talking to customers.

  • Ambiguity and chaos bother you.

  • You want a well-defined research agenda handed to you.

  • You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug.

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount.

Our stack

Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

  1. Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

title: Chief Customer Officer
description:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position 
Work from anywhere!

Position overview

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

The mandate

  1. Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional.
    You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
  2. Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would.
    You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
  3. Win the right members, efficiently.
    You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
  4. Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances.
    Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
  5. Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless.
    You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
  6. Build one Customer organisation, not four.
    Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
  7. Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call.
    You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate

This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

  • You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
  • You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
  • You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
  • You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
  • You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done 

  • 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).
  • Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.
  • Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
  • Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
  • Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
  • Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
  • A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

 

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.
Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.
Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

  • Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
  • Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
  • Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
  • Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.

  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Erfahrung mit Generatorsteuerungen von Vorteil

  • Kenntnisse in der Integration von Anlagen und Systemen

  • Gute Kenntnisse von Stromnetzen, Netzformen und Netzverhalten

  • Sicheres und kundenorientiertes Auftreten

  • Lösungsorientierte und selbstständige Arbeitsweise, Qualitätsbewusstsein

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse, Englisch- und Französischkenntnisse von Vorteil

  • Führerausweis Kategorie B

  • Reisebereitschaft ca. 50 %

  • Pikettdienst

Was Dich auszeichnet

  • Systemisches Denken – Du erkennst Zusammenhänge, auch an Anlagen, die Du nicht selbst gebaut hast

  • Hands-on & pragmatisch – Du bist gerne dort, wo die Anlage steht

Du bist nicht der Typ, der nur tauscht, was kaputt ist. Du verstehst, warum eine Anlage so aufgebaut ist – und sorgst dafür, dass sie auch nach Jahren im Betrieb zuverlässig läuft. Bei uns arbeitest Du an Anlagen, bei denen es zählt, dass sie wirklich laufen.

Du arbeitest an Notstromsystemen, die im Ernstfall funktionieren müssen – kein Spielplatz, sondern echte Verantwortung.

Abwechslung:

Einsätze beim Kunden und Engineering im Haus, etwa zur Hälfte.

Stabilität trifft Wachstum:

Ein etabliertes Unternehmen mit klarer Richtung – und gleichzeitig genug Dynamik, um Dinge wirklich voranzubringen.

title: Homologation & Certification Engineer, Energy Systems
description:
About EH Energy Engineering

EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready.

This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland. We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements, so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate.

 

Key responsibilities

Certification strategy and project management

  • Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine)

  • Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work

  • Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT)

Safety engineering and risk analysis

  • Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882)

  • Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing

  • Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection

  • Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports

Compliance and technical documentation

  • Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports

  • Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling

  • Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards

  • Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates

Collaboration and continuous improvement

  • Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations).

  • Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical)

Standards and regulatory scope

The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required

  • IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

     

Required qualifications

  • Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent

  • 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine)

  • Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110

  • Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs

  • Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard

  • Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts

  • Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508

  • Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals

  • Fluent English, written and spoken

     

Preferred qualifications and personal profile

Nice to have

  • Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects

  • Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED

  • Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification

  • Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification

Personal profile

  • Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail

  • Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving

  • Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers

  • Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end

     

Start date: Immediately

Mollie already uses models in day to day processes, but nobody challenges them independently from a second line perspective yet. As Model Risk Officer, you'll help build the second line model risk function that gives Mollie, and its regulator, confidence that models can be trusted before they're used.

This is a true 0 to 1 role. Mollie isn't a bank today, so there's no model risk framework, validation methodology or model inventory to inherit. You'll design the policy, validation approach and governance from scratch, starting with the credit, IRRBB and capital models already in design for our future capital and liquidity planning. Your work feeds into our licence application and, once authorised, into how we manage model risk every day.

You'll also work with our Machine Learning team and the Domains already deploying models, so you can shape how we manage model risk today, not just in a banking future. Your challenge and sign off will be visible to senior leadership, audit and, eventually, our regulator. As Mollie grows and matures its model risk management, your scope grows from building the framework to running an ongoing model risk cycle.

What you'll ship

  • Build and own Mollie's model risk management framework and policy, including model risk appetite, validation standards and the model risk lifecycle.

  • Set up and maintain the model inventory for credit, IRRBB and capital models, with materiality and risk tiering for each.

  • Coordinate independent second line validation and challenge before models are used, including credit risk and ECL, IRRBB, and Pillar 1 and Pillar 2 capital models.

  • Design the ongoing monitoring and re-validation cycle with the Machine Learning team, covering performance testing, limitation tracking and re-validation triggers.

  • Partner with model owners in Credit Risk and Treasury ALM, and coordinate within the second line Risk function, so model risk challenge is built into the wider risk and capital frameworks.

  • Coordinate clear, well documented validation reports and model risk information that stand up to scrutiny from DNB/ECB, external auditors and internal audit.

What you'll bring

  • Around 5 to 7 years of experience in model risk management or model validation within a bank, preferably across at least one of credit, IRRBB and capital models.

  • Solid working knowledge of ECB model risk expectations and how model validation should be structured and evidenced.

  • Comfort building a model risk framework and validation approach from the ground up. You're excited to write the first playbook.

  • Strong quantitative skills to critically assess model methodology, assumptions and performance, and the discipline to document your findings so others, including a regulator, can follow them.

  • The ability to explain model limitations and validation findings to model owners and senior stakeholders, and the confidence to hold your ground under challenge.

  • Genuine curiosity about how AI can speed up the parts of model validation that don't need a human, so more of your time goes toward judgement and challenge.

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

AI at Mollie

title: Enterprise Applications Manager
description:
Enterprise Applications Manager

About the role

As SkyNRG grows, applications such as SAP Public Cloud, HubSpot, and our Inventory Management System are becoming increasingly important to our operations. We are looking for an Enterprise Applications Manager to take functional ownership of this landscape and ensure our systems effectively support the business.

You will connect business needs with IT solutions, translating requests into clear requirements and coordinated improvements. Working across Commercial, Operations, Maintenance, HSE, Finance and QA, you will create structure, improve adoption and act as the main point of contact for our enterprise applications.

Your key responsibilities include:

  • Take functional ownership of SAP Public Cloud, including EAM and HSE, HubSpot, IMS, and other enterprise applications.

  • Translate business processes and needs into clear requirements, functional designs, user stories and test scenarios.

  • Manage functional support, incidents and change requests, coordinating with external partners and vendors where necessary.

  • Build and maintain the enterprise application roadmap, backlogs and change priorities with IT and business owners.

  • Configure applications within the functional scope and coordinate releases, testing and implementation.

  • Improve application adoption, data quality, reporting and integrations across the application landscape.

  • Maintain process documentation, user guides, application records and access roles in line with security and compliance requirements.

  • Train and support key users across the organization, helping teams make effective use of the available systems.

Your initial focus will include strengthening the use of SAP EAM and HSE, improving HubSpot’s commercial processes and reporting, and introducing a consistent intake and change process for business requests.

While this role does not have direct reports, you will coordinate external implementation partners and application vendors. You will also work closely with the wider IT team to ensure our enterprise applications are reliable, secure and aligned with business priorities.

Your profile

As a growing company in a rapidly evolving industry, we are looking for people who embrace change and are motivated to actively contribute to building and scaling our business. You feel comfortable in an entrepreneurial environment, take ownership, and thrive when things are still developing.

You understand both business processes and enterprise technology. You can move comfortably between conversations with business stakeholders, technical colleagues, and external partners, translating different perspectives into practical solutions. Structured and pragmatic, you take end-to-end responsibility rather than simply passing requests along.

You recognize yourself in the following:

  • A bachelor’s or master’s degree in Business Administration, Information Management, Industrial Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • At least five years of experience as a Business Analyst, Functional Consultant, Application Owner, or in a comparable enterprise applications role.

  • Hands-on functional experience with SAP, ideally SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, in at least one relevant area such as EAM or Plant Maintenance, HSE or EHS, Finance, or Procurement.

  • Experience working with a CRM platform, preferably HubSpot.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate business processes and needs into clear requirements, functional designs, and test scenarios.

  • Experience managing application vendors or implementation partners, including support agreements and service levels.

  • Understanding of change management, release management, testing and access control in an enterprise environment.

  • Strong stakeholder-management and communication skills, with the ability to constructively challenge business requests.

  • Professional fluency in English.

Experience in an industrial, energy, chemical, manufacturing or asset-intensive environment would be an advantage. Familiarity with system integrations, SAP BTP, APIs, Power BI or data-quality initiatives would also be beneficial. Knowledge of relevant regulatory and compliance frameworks, such as NIS2, ISO 27001 and GDPR, is considered a plus.

About SkyNRG

Since 2009, SkyNRG has been a change maker in the aviation industry. We are dedicated to supplying and producing high-integrity Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), making sustainable aviation a reality.

Collaboration is fundamental to achieving our ambition. We nurture genuine relationships with global partners in our drive to make SAF the alternative to fossil jet fuel.

Our in-house team of SAF experts have helped over 60 airlines and corporates reduce their climate impact using the Book & Claim mechanism; the most transparent and traceable way to support aviation sustainability with real emission reductions.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of our company. We maintain an independent Sustainability Board, which advises the company on feedstocks and provides strategic guidance on wide-ranging sustainability issues. SkyNRG operations are certified against the RSB EU RED, CORSIA, and Book & Claim standards.

At SkyNRG, you’ll find:

  • An innovation-driven culture – where big ideas turn into real impact

  • Growth opportunities – in a fast-scaling, industry-changing company

  • A collaborative team – where your ideas and expertise are valued

  • A mission that matters – leading the change in the energy transition by producing and supplying high-integrity SAF

What we offer

We offer a brand-new office in the heart of Amsterdam, designed for collaboration and creativity. Most importantly, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute to a truly game-changing green initiative, making a real impact on the aviation industry and the planet.

Besides that, we offer:

  • 30 paid holidays + 2 for choosing sustainable travel options for your holidays

  • Contribute to a sustainable organization (B Corp)

  • Attractive bonus scheme

  • €5.000,- dedicated budget every 3 years for professional development

  • Commuting travel reimbursement + Lease a Bike plan

  • An office in the city centre of Amsterdam (Nieuwmarkt)

  • Work where it feels best for you: we offer flexible (hybrid in-office) working arrangements

  • Generous employer pension contribution

  • Paid Volunteering Day

  • Access to our electric company boat (also available for private use), free lunch, and lots of social activities – all part of the deal!

Is this you?

Are you ready to take the next step in your career with SkyNRG? Explore our vacancies and become part of our company of change makers. Together, we can change the future of flying.

For more information about SkyNRG visit www.skynrg.com.

As one of the leading companies in Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), SkyNRG is developing and advancing projects, partnerships and commercial opportunities that will play a critical role in the decarbonization of aviation.

As our portfolio grows in scale and complexity, we are looking to further strengthen our investment capabilities, combining strategic thinking, commercial insight and disciplined decision-making to accelerate value creation across the business. To support this next stage of growth, we are seeking a Chief Investment Officer.

Reporting directly to the CEO and working closely with the Executive Committee, Board and shareholders, the CIO will play a central role in shaping the future direction of SkyNRG. This executive will bring an institutional investor mindset to the organization, strengthening how opportunities are evaluated, prioritized and executed while ensuring that capital is deployed toward initiatives that create sustainable strategic and financial value.

The Opportunity

The Chief Investment Officer will be responsible for leading SkyNRG's Investment Management capability and driving value creation across the business.

Working closely with the Executive Committee, Board and shareholders, the CIO will help shape the strategic direction of SkyNRG by ensuring investment decisions, capital allocation and growth initiatives are aligned with long-term value creation.

This role combines the analytical rigor of an investment professional with the strategic perspective of a business leader. It offers the opportunity to influence some of the most significant decisions facing the company while contributing directly to the development of projects and partnerships that support the future of sustainable aviation.

Your Role

As Chief Investment Officer, you will be responsible for strengthening investment decision-making and value creation across SkyNRG.

You will:

  • Lead SkyNRG's Investment Management capability and establish the frameworks, governance and standards that support disciplined decision-making.

  • Further improve SkyNRG’s investment strategy, building on 17 years of SAF experience, network and track record, and the company’s overall strategic plans

  • Drive the evaluation and prioritization of major investments, strategic partnerships and growth opportunities across the portfolio.

  • Bring an institutional investor mindset into the organization, fostering collaboration across teams and ensuring opportunities are assessed through the lens of strategic fit, risk-adjusted returns and long-term value creation.

  • Provide leadership to Corporate Development and Project Commercial activities, building high-performing teams and fostering a collaborative, results-driven culture that aligns strategic ambitions, commercial execution and investment outcomes.

  • Support the development of bankable, financeable and commercially attractive SAF projects.

  • Lead selected M&A, partnership and corporate development opportunities that contribute to SkyNRG's long-term growth strategy.

  • Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Executive Committee, Board and shareholders on investment strategy, capital allocation and portfolio prioritization.

Key Areas of Impact

Investment Strategy

You will provide leadership on how capital is allocated across SkyNRG's portfolio, ensuring resources are directed toward opportunities with the greatest strategic and commercial potential.

You will oversee investment evaluations, valuation methodologies, business case development and portfolio prioritization to support informed decision-making at Executive Committee and Board level.

Portfolio Development

You will help maximize value across SkyNRG's portfolio by strengthening investment discipline throughout the project lifecycle.

From opportunity identification through commercial structuring and execution, you will ensure investment decisions are supported by robust analysis, clear governance and a strong understanding of risk and value drivers.

Partnerships

Growth opportunities are expected to come from a combination of project development, strategic partnerships and selective corporate development initiatives.

You will play a leading role in identifying, assessing and executing opportunities that enhance SkyNRG's position within the sustainable aviation ecosystem and support the company's long-term ambitions.

Organizational Leadership

You will collaborate closely with teams across Projects, Commercial, Finance, Legal and Strategy to strengthen how investment opportunities are evaluated and executed.

By embedding a common investment framework across the business, you will increase transparency, improve decision quality and support a culture focused on value creation and accountability.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for a strategic and collaborative leader with a strong track record in investment, infrastructure, energy or related capital-intensive industries. You are able to build trust across diverse stakeholder groups and bring people together around complex decisions.

You combine strategic thinking with strong commercial judgment and have experience evaluating complex investment opportunities in capital-intensive environments.

You are comfortable influencing senior stakeholders, engaging with boards and shareholders and navigating situations where commercial, financial and strategic considerations intersect.

You bring:

  • 15+ years of relevant experience in infrastructure, energy transition, project finance, private equity, corporate development or investment management.

  • A proven track record of evaluating and executing complex investment opportunities.

  • Deep expertise in valuation, financial analysis, capital allocation and investment decision-making.

  • Experience working with executive teams, Boards and institutional investors.

  • Strong leadership and stakeholder management capabilities.

  • The ability to balance strategic vision with pragmatic execution.

  • A genuine interest in accelerating the transition toward more sustainable aviation.

We recognize that exceptional candidates may not meet every listed requirement. If you are excited about the opportunity to shape the future of sustainable aviation and believe your experience can contribute to our ambitions, we encourage you to apply.

Location & International Exposure

Based at SkyNRG's Amsterdam headquarters, this role offers the opportunity to work across an international network of partners, investors and project stakeholders that are helping shape the future of sustainable aviation.

We offer a flexible hybrid working model, recognizing that impactful leadership can be delivered through a combination of in-person collaboration, stakeholder engagement and remote working.

Why join SkyNRG

This is an opportunity to play a defining role in one of the most dynamic and ambitious companies operating within the sustainable aviation sector.

As Chief Investment Officer, you will influence investment decisions that shape the future of the company, contribute to the development of large-scale SAF projects and help create long-term value for shareholders, partners and the aviation industry as a whole.

You will join an entrepreneurial and mission-driven organization where commercial success and sustainable impact go hand in hand, and where your decisions will directly influence the growth trajectory of both the business and the broader SAF ecosystem.

Is this you?

Are you ready to take the next step in your career with SkyNRG? Explore our vacancies and become part of our company of change makers. Together, we can change the future of flying.

title: People Business Partner
description:
About myTomorrows 

myTomorrows is a global health tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers for patients seeking treatment options.   

We strive to enable earlier and better treatment access by bridging the gap between those searching for possible options, and the companies who develop them. We work closely with patients, healthcare professionals, trial sites, patient advocacy groups, and BioPharma – connecting key stakeholders in the drug development ecosystem.   

We’ve developed a cutting-edge AI-powered technology platform that simplifies and streamlines access to drugs in development. To support our users and clients, we have a range of industry-expert specialized teams ready to help. With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. Join us in shaping the future of treatment access - making tomorrow’s therapies accessible for people who need them today.

As a People Business Partner at myTomorrows, you are a trusted advisor to senior leaders and the Leadership Team. In this Individual contributor People Business Partner role, you will translate business priorities into practical people solutions that enable high performing teams and organizational growth.

You will partner closely with leaders across the organization to strengthen leadership effectiveness, organizational design, performance, engagement, and talent development. Given that most of our team is located in the Netherlands, we only consider candidates who live within commuting distance of our Amsterdam office.

What you'll do in this role:

  • Coach leaders on performance management, leadership effectiveness, feedback, development, and difficult people conversations.

  • Translate business strategy into practical People initiatives that support organizational growth and scalability.

  • Use people data and insights to identify trends, challenge assumptions, and recommend actions that improve engagement, retention, and organizational performance.

  • Partner closely with Talent Acquisition and People Operations to deliver an outstanding employee experience across the entire employee lifecycle.

  • Ensure consistent application of People policies, employment legislation, and People practices across your business areas.

  • Lead cross functional People projects that improve organizational effectiveness, manager capability, and operational excellence.

  • Act as a trusted sparring partner who balances strategic thinking with hands on execution.

What you bring to the table:

  • At least 5 years of progressive HR experience or experience as a People Business Partner in a fast growing international organization.

  • Demonstrated experience partnering with senior leaders on organizational and people topics.

  • Extensive experience managing complex employee relations, performance management, and organizational change.

  • Strong coaching, influencing, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Solid knowledge of Dutch employment law and HR best practices.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate people data into actionable business insights.

  • Comfortable operating independently, making sound judgments, and managing competing priorities.

  • Experience working in a technology, SaaS, HealthTech, or scale up environment is highly preferred.

  • Experience with modern HR systems such as Personio is a plus.

  • Experience supporting international teams is a plus.

What we offer:

  • Serve a purposeful mission by helping patients gain access to potentially lifesaving treatments.

  • International work environment with scale up energy and a flat organization.

  • Competitive salary, annual performance bonus, and equity.

  • Great career development opportunities in a growing company.

  • Learning and development budget alongside internal knowledge sharing sessions.

  • Attractive pension plan with the full premium covered by us.

  • Hybrid working model.

  • Policies that support working parents.

  • Healthy lunch at the office.

  • Unlimited access to professional guidance by certified psychologists through OpenUp.

  • An additional holiday every year to celebrate Liberation Day on May 5.

Equal opportunities

myTomorrows is an Equal Opportunity Employer and, beyond upholding discrimination-free practices, we are committed to cultivating a workplace where difference and diversity are protected and celebrated. The best work comes from our best selves, and we go to great lengths in supporting our team members to be just that.

title: Mandatory Internship Overall Aircraft Design (all genders)
description:
Your Mission:

Be part of aviation history at VÆRIDION, where we’re pioneering the world’s first electric nine-seater aircraft! As an Overall Aircraft Design Intern (all genders), you will join our Central Engineering team and support across various Overall Aircraft Design activities. This role is a broad role, and you will perform different tasks to support on-going aircraft design and analysis activities. You will be part of our interdisciplinary aircraft design team and contribute directly to the design process of our battery-electric aircraft.

 

Your Day-to-Day:

  • Support the analysis and comparison of battery-electric aircraft concepts across different configurations and mission profiles.

  • Investigate how technology assumptions and key design parameters influence aircraft performance, energy demand, and overall feasibility.

  • Develop and adapt computational tools to support aircraft sizing, mission analysis, and design trade-off studies.

  • Perform parameter and sensitivity studies to explore design dependencies and identify key technology drivers.

  • Collect, assess, and organise technical data to support consistent modelling assumptions and comparative analyses.

  • Document methods, assumptions, and results, and prepare clear visualisations to discuss findings with the engineering team.

Your Profile:

  • Currently enrolled in a Master’s degree programme in Aerospace Engineering or a comparable technical discipline.

  • Holding a Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering or a comparable technical discipline.

  • Excellent programming skills (e.g., Python, MATLAB).

  • Experience with aircraft design process, methods and tools. Experience with dedicated tools such as OpenMDAO and Aviary is a strong plus.

  • Readily available knowledge about aircraft.

  • Structured, analytical, and solution-oriented professional with strong ownership, facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; additional European languages are an asset, combined with a strong motivation for aviation and electric aircraft technologies.

We recognize that women and other under-represented groups are often overlooked in our industry. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every listed qualification, we still encourage you to apply. Talent and potential can’t always be captured in a checklist.

 

Why us?

  • Be part of an ambitious team determined to shape the future of aviation.

  • We are an in-office company, but we value flexibility and trust employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work or adjusting hours to accommodate personal commitments.

  • Subsidized EGYM Wellpass membership: your (mental) health is important for us.

  • Become a part of our success with virtual stock options.

  • Choose the option that suits your needs: either a free charging station for your electric car or a public transport job ticket as part of the Deutschlandticket.

  • Lease a high-quality bicycle or e-bike through our JobRad program and benefit from tax advantages. Whether for your daily commute or personal use, enjoy more mobility and sustainability.

  • Pension scheme to support your long-term financial security.

  • Work in one of our offices in Munich or Delft. Enjoy the modern Balan Campus in Munich or work close to the innovative Aerospace TU Delft.

  • Boost your professional as well as personal growth executing your own ideas and independent projects.

  • Join our internal social events and retreats (e.g. cooking, game nights, sports).

VÆRIDION was founded in 2021 to transform regional air travel with the Microliner, a 100% electric commercial aircraft. By delivering the most energy-efficient aircraft, we are building the future where clean, safe, and affordable electric aviation seamlessly connects people and businesses. We’re bringing together the brightest minds in aerospace, automotive engineering, and business to disrupt the aviation industry.

title: Commercial Account Executive (Benelux)
Senior Engineer, QA
Senior Engineer I, Software Engineering
Director Go-to-Market and Revenue Strategy
description:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a commercial leader who has built the go-to-market of a platform from a blank page and knows what it takes to turn a product that people already use into a business that pays for itself. You have priced and packaged products for marketplaces, brands or merchants, and you have seen the difference between a model that looks good in a spreadsheet and one that a small business owner actually adopts.

You are comfortable in a B2B2C world: the customer is reached through someone else's channel, the data belongs to the ecosystem, and the money comes from several ends of a transaction at once. You influence without authority, because the teams that execute will rarely report to you. You are rigorous with numbers and plain with people, and you are at ease saying what the evidence shows even when the room expects something else.

You want to build something that reaches millions of small businesses, you are prepared to work for it.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Toqan for Partners is the AI assistant for the merchants across the companies of the Prosus ecosystem: restaurants, pharmacies, hotels, sellers, real estate agencies and car dealers, five million businesses in total. It launched to restaurants on iFood in Brazil in September 2026 and reached 65,000 restaurants in four weeks with no media spend.

The next twelve months decide how it will become a business: which applications partners pay for and at what price, how value is shared with everyone the partner transacts with, how the uplift is measured and published so the next company embeds, and how the product travels from iFood to the rest of the ecosystem and to India and Europe. You will lead that work, as the owner of the go-to-market and the revenue strategy of Toqan for Partners, alongside the product and technology leads who own what gets built.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Own the commercial model

Define pricing and packaging for the applications partners pay for, media management, supply, finance and operations, at a fraction of what they spend today and justified by the return they see. Design how Toqan takes part in the value it creates for the other end: take rate on agent-negotiated supply, credit origination, brand and industry media, and cross-sell of the ecosystem companies' own products. Set the rules that keep it honest, starting with the separation between paid placement and recommendation.

Drive the rollout across the ecosystem

With the Head of Operations, secure the commitment of each business in the ecosystem: sponsor, distribution, conditional yes and first market. Run the rollout inside each one, working through the teams that own the merchant relationship, and bring the product to its next verticals and markets.

Build the measurement

Own the scoreboard: active partners under a strict definition, uplift per business in retention and GMV, cost and value per active partner. Make the uplift the argument that brings the next company in and the evidence behind every pricing decision.

Structure the partnerships that carry the revenue

Lead the commercial agreements with distributors, industry, fintechs and the ecosystem companies' commercial platforms, from first conversation to signed terms, and the co-investment models that align their incentives with the partner's.

Build and lead the team

Hire and develop a small go-to-market and revenue team, growth on the merchant side, monetisation and analytics, and set its standard for rigour, ownership and candour.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Ten or more years in go-to-market, revenue or commercial strategy, with at least one commercial function built from scratch and grown to scale.

  • Hands-on experience with pricing and packaging, ideally for marketplaces, retail media, payments or SaaS sold to small businesses.

  • Experience on more than one side of a marketplace: merchants or sellers, brands or suppliers, the platform itself.

  • A track record of adoption at scale with a long tail of small customers, not only of large enterprise deals.

  • Proven ability to move a result through teams that do not report to you, and to work inside another company's channel.

  • Fluency with data: you build the business case, run the analysis and read the uplift yourself, and use AI tooling as a normal part of how you work.

  • Candour, humility and patience: you say what the numbers say, you arrive to learn before you teach.

  • English required; Portuguese or Spanish strongly preferred.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Global impact: a product that reaches five million small businesses across Latin America, Europe and India.

  • Ownership: the commercial model of a new business, with the numbers to be judged on and the autonomy to build it.

  • Growth: exposure to the leadership of the group and of its companies, and a clear path into operating roles in the ecosystem.

  • Competitive compensation and the Prosus benefits package for the location of the role.

Why Prosus?

description:

We nurture innovation and an inspiring work environment where bold ideas thrive, prioritizing thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and our business as a whole.
 
Maintaining our start-up spirit, we prioritize thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and, of course, our business.

About The Role

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst, Lifecycle to own measurement and experimentation for how new customers activate and existing ones stay.The metrics are yours whatever the lever: CRM campaigns, promos and incentives, onboarding changes in the product, and a next best action layer that decides what each customer should see next. You decide what we test, how we test it and what we do with the answer. You also bring your own hypotheses on where the next win is.

 


What You'll Do

What you'll do

Join activation and retention initiatives before anything is built, whether they come from CRM, growth or product. Define the primary metric, check against historical data whether the effect is detectable at our volumes, and turn solution-shaped requests into problem-shaped ones.

Design and analyse experiments end to end: hypothesis, guardrails, audience split, MDE and power, stopping rule, and a readout that ends in ship, iterate or kill. 

Correct for channel and engagement bias (not everyone opens email, and open and click populations are self-selected). When a clean A/B is impossible, use causal inference: diff-in-diff, matching, synthetic control or geo designs.

Bring hypotheses of your own. Launch a few new experiments across onboarding and the customer lifecycle, and turn one-off wins into recurring segmented flows.

Build deliberately simple models: segmentation, propensity, churn and dormancy scoring. They feed audiences, personalisation and incentive targeting. Over time these come together into next best action: for a given customer, which offer, feature nudge or message to send next, through which channel, and whether to send anything at all. You own the logic and the measurement of whether it beats the current rules.

Automate your own recurring work: audience refresh jobs, readout templates, dashboards for Activation, Onboarding and Retention. Ship models the Databricks way (scheduled jobs write tables, tables map into downstream tools such as Braze) and bring engagement data back into the warehouse to close the loop.


What You Bring

What you bring

  • Strong SQL and Python, and a Git-based warehouse workflow with code review.

  • Experiment design, statistics and metric design you can defend.

  • BI experience, Power BI/Tableau or similar.

  • Stakeholder management and business sense: you can push back, reframe a request and land a recommendation with a non-technical audience.

  • Curiosity and ownership. You run your area without waiting to be asked.

    •  


    Nice To Have

    Nice to have

  • Causal inference methods and a clear sense of when each one is valid.

  • Clustering and segmentation that ends up in use, not in a slide.

  • Predictive modelling with honest validation. Uplift modelling is a plus.

  • Braze or a comparable CRM platform: audiences, canvases, native split testing, channel mechanics and their biases.

    • What You Will Get In Return

    Join our upward trajectory, and grow with us. We provide the resources and opportunities for continuous personal and professional development, empowering you to make a genuine impact on our evolving product.

    Unlock your inner entrepreneur and align your aspirations with ours through our Stock Options Program. This exciting opportunity is available to every team member, from junior team members to our founders.

    Finom stands by you at every step, embodying our commitment to your well-being and success reflected in our modern, friendly, and eco-conscious corporate culture. We offer constant support and care to ensure your Finom experience is successful and fulfilling.

  • Op de hoogte blijven van ontwikkelingen in data en AI en die vertalen naar onze dienstverlening.

Projectleiding

  • Datamanagementtrajecten van start tot finish leiden, binnen tijd, budget en kwaliteit.

  • Projectplannen opstellen, voortgang bewaken en samenwerken met data engineers, analisten en andere consultants.

Business development

  • Meedenken over proposities en use cases, en kansen signaleren via je netwerk.

  • Bijdragen aan voorstellen en presentaties voor nieuwe klanten, samen met het salesteam.


Wat jij meebrengt

  • Bachelor of Master in Bedrijfskunde, Informatiekunde, Computerwetenschappen of een verwant vakgebied.

  • Minimaal 3 jaar relevante ervaring in een dataomgeving, bijvoorbeeld als data-analist of als consultant met focus op datamanagement.

  • Minimaal 2 jaar ervaring in consultancy, bij voorkeur bij een gerenommeerd adviesbureau.

  • Goed begrip van datamanagementconcepten, zoals data governance en datastrategie.

  • Ervaring met het leiden van complexe projecten.

  • Je gebruikt AI zelf in je werk en hebt zin om samen met ons te ontdekken wat er nog meer kan.

  • Sterke communicatieve vaardigheden: je betrekt en beïnvloedt stakeholders op alle niveaus.

  • Flexibel en leergierig: je schakelt makkelijk tussen klanten, omgevingen en onderwerpen.

  • Vloeiend Nederlands en Engels, mondeling en schriftelijk.

Nice-to-have: kennis van AI-governance en data-readiness voor AI, en commercieel inzicht.

Waarom adesso? Omdat je bij ons écht kunt meebouwen.

Bij adesso Nederland draait het om meer dan alleen technologie. We bouwen slimme oplossingen die daadwerkelijk waarde toevoegen voor onze klanten. Geen eindeloze experimenten of AI omdat het hip is, maar technologie die werkt en impact maakt.

We zijn onderdeel van de internationale adesso Group, met ruim 11.500 collega's op meer dan 60 locaties. Tegelijkertijd zijn we in Nederland een relatief klein en persoonlijk team, met korte lijnen, veel vrijheid en ruimte voor eigen initiatief.

Groot genoeg om impact te maken, klein genoeg om het verschil te voelen.

AI First: samen bouwen aan de toekomst

Bij adesso Nederland ontwikkelen we ons tot een AI First-organisatie. We geloven dat AI de manier waarop we software ontwikkelen, met data werken en klanten helpen fundamenteel verandert.

Daarom kijken we verder dan losse AI-experimenten. We bouwen aan slimme dataplatformen, AI-first applicaties en agentic oplossingen die écht onderdeel worden van bedrijfsprocessen.

Dat betekent ook dat we onze eigen manier van werken blijven vernieuwen. We omarmen nieuwe technologie, maar blijven kritisch: niet alles hoeft met AI. De beste oplossing staat altijd voorop.


En misschien wel het belangrijkste: de mensen

We houden van collega's die nieuwsgierig zijn, kennis delen en elkaar verder helpen. Mensen die goed zijn in hun vak, maar ook plezier hebben in samenwerken. Je krijgt bij ons vertrouwen, verantwoordelijkheid en de vrijheid om ideeën daadwerkelijk uit te voeren.

Wat krijg je van ons?

Zullen we kennismaken?

Je hoeft niet aan ieder technisch punt te voldoen. We zijn vooral benieuwd naar wat je hebt gebouwd, welke keuzes je hebt gemaakt en waar je naartoe wilt groeien.

Een cv of LinkedIn-profiel is genoeg om het gesprek te starten. Daarna volgen een kennismaking, een technisch gesprek en een praktijkcase.
